Every time I meet someone I ask a seemingly innocuous, incredibly simple question: "What do you do?"

Most people assume I am asking the question "What do you do professionally?" and answer with their occupation. However, the reason I ask this question is to determine how the individual thinks and what they value. I love the answers that aren't related at all to professions, but rather focus on how people spend their free time.

"What are some of your favorite books?"

The only real danger sign would be if they can't think of any.

What you will learn about their character doesn't so much come from the specifics, but from whether and how they can discuss this question. "I don't read" — run away. Can they name a few? Good. Do they say they like so many books it's hard to choose? Great. Are the books they like completely different from the books you like, and they're willing to argue literary tastes for hours? Jackpot.

I can think a of a few books that might make me back away, but, really, the difference between not reading and being passionate about ANY books (even that one with the sparkly vampires; yes, even that one that started as fanfiction about the one about the sparkly vampires) is much more important that whatever differences we may have about which books we like.

Tell me about your last break up/why you left your last job.

For me, this reveals a lot about how the person handles adversity, how they hold grudges, whether they shift blame and mostly, whether they are a positive or negative personality. I don't care for buzzkill personalities at all.
